questions: Did these episodes begin after the child was given metoclopramide, domperidone, prochlorperazine, or another medicine for vomiting?
During the episode, is the child unresponsive or unable to respond normally?
Does the child have repeated episodes of upward eye deviation with tongue protrusion?
Has the child had any generalized shaking or loss of consciousness?
Do the episodes consist of sustained upward or sideways deviation of both eyes with the child remaining conscious and responsive?
Do the episodes last minutes to hours and recur several times per day?
Are the episodes triggered or worsened by fatigue, illness, emotional stress, or excitement?
Is the child completely normal between episodes?
Did the episodes begin during infancy, before the age of one year?
Has the child had delayed motor or language development?
Does the child have persistent low muscle tone or weakness between episodes?
Does the child have involuntary twisting or stiffening of the neck, trunk, arms, or legs?
During episodes, does the child have sweating, irritability, nasal congestion, or difficulty sleeping?
Has the child had feeding difficulty, choking, or poor weight gain since infancy?
Are the abnormal eye movements accompanied by sustained tongue protrusion or other abnormal mouth movements?
Has the child lost previously acquired skills or developed repetitive hand-wringing or hand-to-mouth movements?
orders: Prolonged video-electroencephalography (EEG) monitoring with simultaneous recording of the typical eye-deviation episodes
Comprehensive pediatric ophthalmologic examination, including assessment for nystagmus, saccades, ocular alignment, and funduscopy
Brain MRI with attention to the brainstem, cerebellum, and basal ganglia
served: nystagmus: direction and whether it changes with gaze
abducting nystagmus of the fellow eye
